rejected_experiment.label: signed-depth-zone1

warnings: WARNING: Screen-space AA is only available when using the Forward+ or Mobile renderer.

rejected_experiment.conclusion: Paired land/water vertex depth is not a safe wet mask: horizontal displacement and coverage changes cause dry-ground lighting. A vertical wave margin leaves 55 dry pixels in one wind view and 231 in a raised-water view. Do not restore this approximation.
rejected_experiment.fixture_limit: The initial probe carried wave state between successive views and chose the second focus after raised water. Its rest/wind labels do not form an independent timing comparison. It still establishes actual false-wet receivers in that frozen state; final probes reset wave state for every case and capture both foci before changing levels.

test_interface_note: The final zone15 run replaces the earlier final-lake run after renaming its diagnostic switch from --caustic-lake to --caustic-zone15. The sampled zone15 scene is a water-filled canyon. Other final test bodies are unchanged; snapshots preserve their exact tool source.
limitations: Conservative, view-independent receiver mask, not exact instantaneous liquid depth or a wave/refraction simulation. Homogeneous material rings intentionally omit narrow pools and mixed edges; minimum heights attenuate steep flows.

Metadata assumes immutable, axis-aligned authored terrain/water meshes with the existing 9-vertex tile layout. Dynamic water levels and bounded original waves are supported. Arbitrary runtime water topology/material edits or transformed terrain require rebuilding/adapting the field.

Terrain receivers only. Existing underwater attenuation and shadowing still shade the multiplied albedo. Sun gating is global, following the reference behavior; this is not optical focusing or an added per-pixel sunlight occlusion calculation.

Four metadata fetches and two mipmapped pattern samples in the opt-in nearby sunlit terrain variant, plus live phase bindings to resident terrain materials. No measured GPU/frame-time/device benefit is claimed.

Graphics runs are Linux RTX 3090 with the previously patched runtime. Other Godot processes were recorded at many boundaries, so observed field/enable times are diagnostic, not controlled performance evidence.

The visual fixtures are two water-filled map channels, not whole-map or real co-op routes. Wider shorelines, viewpoints, underwater-camera play, deformed terrain, Android/web cost and artistic acceptance remain open.
Lava/swamp/emission checks deliberately change classification metadata in the fixture. They establish exclusion logic, not broad visual coverage of all non-water maps.

Wave-equation propagation, current advection, refraction changes and waterfall shells/spray/mist remain separate unimplemented V4 adaptations. V2 ground cover is next in the initial visual sequence; gameplay U45 remains first when entering the gameplay track.
